about: Contract items that specs must cite and must not resolve, with the record of how each was closed. Maintained by hand through internal:governance PRs. tools/scope_trace.py reads `gates` and `contradictions`; A resolved contradiction may list `engineering_ids`, which the checker lets a spec trace with every dependent criterion `pending CX-nn`. `working_decisions` is the record of owner decisions on open client items (DECISIONS.md D-10) and is read by people, not by the checker.

CX-01.title: Accountant role: narrative says it exists at launch, the row says DEF
evidence: Register v1.5 line 224 (Part One 1.3, ROLE-06a): 'The Accountant role itself exists at launch (ROLE-06)'
Register v1.5 lines 774-779 (blockquote 'On the Accountant role'): 'the role and its permission profile exist at launch (ROLE-06)'
Register v1.5 line 767 (ROLE-06 row): scope DEF, stage '-'
Register v1.5 line 358 (Part One 1.6): ROLE-06 replaced by 'The standard commerce role set' (ROLE-09)
Client Scope Summary lines 194 and 319: Accountant profile listed as not included
Functional Specification v1.2: stories written 'As the accountant' (lines 1143, 1165, 2584, 3141) while carrying ROLE-06 as DEF
CX-01.affects: Which staff roles hold 'financial permission', for example US-16-05 AC2 (product cost visibility).
CX-01.route: Stage 1 review with the client. Raised by Mustafa. Not resolved in code, criteria or governance.

resolution.decided_by: Mustafa Shaaban, as owner of the engagement
resolution.decision: The Accountant role exists at launch. Where the ROLE-06 row and the register's own narrative disagree, the reading that favours the client is taken: the narrative promises the role twice in plain words.
permissions: Least privilege. Financial permission is held by Owner / Super Admin, by Admin where appropriate, and by the Accountant for its accounting and financial responsibilities.

The Accountant covers the Stage 1 financial functions it needs: payment and financial visibility, invoices, product cost where permitted, and reconciliation information inside contracted Stage 1 scope.
The Accountant holds no general administration: no plugin, theme or file management, no user or role administration, no unrelated system configuration.
Refund permission is a separate granular capability. Being an Accountant does not grant it.
resolution.history: The contradiction is kept as evidence above and is not rewritten. It was open from ratification (22 September 2026) to this decision.
resolution.contract_instrument: Outstanding. A Scope Clarification and Register Correction, MS-CLR-2026-037, is drafted for the client's acknowledgement and is not acknowledged. The signed register is not edited. ROLE-06 still reads DEF there and in register-ids.json. ROLE-06a stays P2: the advanced reports arrive later.
resolution.engineering_note: D-11: engineering proceeds under this resolution. A spec may trace ROLE-06 while it still reads DEF, and every criterion that cites it is `pending CX-01`, never final or provisional. That is not contractual acceptance: acceptance of ROLE-06 waits for the client's acknowledgement of the Scope Clarification and for the register to carry the row as an obligation.

capability_policy.decided: 2026-10-05, D-11, Mustafa. The launch policy unless an exact signed row contradicts it. Implemented as granular capabilities, so it can be adjusted without rebuilding roles. The exact capability matrix is recorded in the roles PBI, #251.
Admin: operational financial visibility needed to manage orders
product cost where the contracted admin role needs it
refund capability where the launch refund flow permits it
Accountant: financial reporting actually present at launch

working_decisions.about: Owner-approved working and delivery decisions. None is a client confirmation, and none is to be described as one unless the client later confirms it explicitly. A criterion that rests on one is `provisional` or `pending OD-nn`, never `final` (M-10).

OD-27.title: Hosting outside Egypt
OD-27.decision: Not decided, and not recorded as client-approved. Development and the staging and demonstration environment run on the developer's own machine, with synthetic data only, so OD-27 no longer blocks development or staging verification.
OD-27.still_gates: Production infrastructure and launch: the contract requires the client's written instruction before production hosting is provisioned (R-03, CR-10).

OD-14.title: Monthly operating budget for hosting and services
OD-14.decision: Not decided. It is a production hosting and budget gate, not a development blocker.

OD-15.title: Expected product count, order volume and traffic
OD-15.decision: Starting sizing baseline of 5,000 products. The architecture supports growth beyond 5,000 without redesign. The 300 orders a day planning assumption stays until testing or evidence requires a revision.
OD-15.still_gates: Nothing in development. Production sizing is confirmed with OD-14.

OD-19.title: Payment methods at launch
OD-19.decision: Launch-capable payment methods are cards and mobile wallets. Provider credentials or activation do not block payment architecture or development.
OD-19.still_gates: Activation of wallets at launch depends on the payment provider and the merchant account (PAY-15).

OD-21.title: Tracking integrations at launch
OD-21.decision: Google Analytics with Tag Manager, Meta and TikTok are all in the launch tracking plan, where the contracted Stage 1 rows require them.
OD-21.still_gates: Provider and account setup is an integration and launch input.

OD-03.title: Welcome discount
OD-03.decision: Example default, admin-configurable under BR-001: 10 percent off the first order, capped at 200 EGP, minimum order 500 EGP, valid 14 days from account creation, one use, new customers only, not combined with other coupons.
OD-03.still_gates: The client's real values, set in the admin before launch.

OD-04.title: Free shipping: what two items means
OD-04.decision: Two or more units in the cart, any mix of products, no exclusions. The condition stays admin-configurable under BR-002.
OD-04.still_gates: The client's confirmation of the rule before launch.

OD-05.title: Cash on delivery
OD-05.decision: The cash on delivery capability is built and tested as PAY-09 requires: native, with a configurable switch, and restricted by shipping method or zone where that is native. D-11: no value ceiling and no fee is contracted. No PAY, CHK, ADM or BR row supports one, so neither is built, and either would be a later scope decision. The example limit and fee recorded under D-10 are withdrawn.
OD-05.still_gates: The launch switch stays the client's: PAY-09 is enabled at launch only if the client selects it.
